what_worked: Consistent visual identity and polished graphic design throughout the deck.
fix_next: This is a meta-presentation about how to present data, not a data story from the assigned dataset—it contains zero analysis of the dataset.
verdict: Wrong assignment: a design philosophy lecture with no dataset analysis whatsoever.
factual_error_detail: No dataset claims are made, so no factual errors against the dataset—but the entire deck fails to engage with the required data.

evidence.insight: All 15 slides discuss presentation philosophy (visual metaphors, cognitive load, action titles). Zero insights derived from the 1,000-row dataset. No revenue, category, provider, or any other dataset finding appears anywhere.
evidence.narrative: The deck has internal coherence as a design-principles lecture (pillars → techniques → protocol → closing), but this narrative is entirely off-topic for the assignment. No thesis about the dataset exists.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 frames this as 'Transforming raw data into strategic visual narratives for the C-Suite'—a generic meta-topic. No mention of the actual dataset, its scope, its questions, or any analytical context. A cold reader would not know what data was assigned.
evidence.accuracy: No dataset figures are cited anywhere across 15 slides. The '60,000x faster' claim on slide 3 is a widely debunked marketing statistic presented without citation. Slide 8's comparison table uses fabricated dot-ratings with no empirical basis. No calculations, no denominators, no sample sizes.
evidence.visual: Slides are visually polished with consistent blueprint/orange theme, good typography hierarchy, and varied layouts (pillars, funnel, Venn, heatmap, matrix). However, every graphic is decorative/conceptual rather than evidence-led. No actual data chart appears in the entire deck.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy AI slop throughout: inflated consulting language ('cognitive resonance,' 'narrative architecture,' 'engineering the visual consumption'), decorative 3D renders on slides 1/15, generic frameworks (pillars, flywheels, Venn diagrams) with no dataset-specific content, and the entire deck reads as a generic AI-generated presentation-design tutorial that could apply to any context.
